summary: Yangdon Dhondup is a tibetologist who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London between circa 1999 and 2004, supervised by Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen works in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under Yongdong Shi, and also studied under the traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Yanpei (1917–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Taixu from circa 1934 to 1940 and under Yin Shun from circa 1941 to 1947.
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. He studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of California by 1997 and has served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xueyu (attested 2010).

Yaroslav Komarovski is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at several institutes, monasteries, and the University of Virginia. He held a Mellon postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

Yaroslav Vassilkov is an Indologist who studied at St. Petersburg University's Faculty of Oriental Studies (~1962–1967). He held posts at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (~1974) and the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University.

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Yasuaki Nara studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Calcutta under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno. He held multiple posts at Komazawa University, including professor emeritus and president, and directed the Soto Zen Research Center.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD). He held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology, UC Berkeley, Toyo Bunko, NIHU, and Sokendai.
Yasuhiko Sueki is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He later served as a professor emeritus at Komazawa University.

Yasuhiro Okazaki is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. He held posts at Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda, Kabe Senior, and Takamiya high schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki is a Buddhist studies scholar who undertook short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library. He held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, serving as vice director.
Yasuhiro Ueno works in Buddhist studies. He undertook doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004) and held a research post at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki (1929–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as an associate professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1980–2000).

Indologist Yasuke Ikari studied at Kyoto University and the University of Chicago (PhD) under Masaaki Hattori. He held academic posts at Kyoto University from 1973 until becoming professor emeritus in 2004, alongside appointments at Kindai University, Minpaku, and Harvard.

Yasumasa Sekine is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS, he held faculty posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasuo Deguchi is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Nagoya Institute of Technology before serving as associate professor, professor, and dean at Kyoto University, and later joined ZEN University.

Yasuo Goto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer and part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991, 2006) and as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

Yasuo Inamoto works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1995–2007) and took up a post at Kyoto University circa 2007.
